## Getting started

Source: [doc/getting-started.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/seifalmotaz/tanstack-ai-dart/main/doc/getting-started.md)

## Connect your first chat

You need Dart at the minimum version listed in the [README](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/seifalmotaz/tanstack-ai-dart/main/README.md), a
compatible backend, and any credentials that backend requires. The SDK does not
select a model, create backend routes, or supply provider credentials.

### Install and configure

1. Add the Git dependency from the README while the package is unpublished.
2. Run `dart pub get`.
3. Pass your chat route URL to `fetchServerSentEvents`.
4. Add authentication with a fixed header or an async options provider. See
   [connections and authentication](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/seifalmotaz/tanstack-ai-dart/main/doc/connections.md).

### Run a request

This function is maintained in [basic_chat.dart](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/seifalmotaz/tanstack-ai-dart/main/example/basic_chat.dart).
Call `runChat` with your application's backend URL.

<!-- example: example/basic_chat.dart -->
```dart
import 'package:tanstack_ai_dart/tanstack_ai_dart.dart';

Future<void> runChat(String endpoint) async {
  final client = ChatClient(
    connection: fetchServerSentEvents(endpoint),
    threadId: 'conversation-123',
  );
  final subscription = client.states.listen((snapshot) {
    for (final message in snapshot.messages) {
      print('${message.role}: ${message.answer}');
    }
  });

  try {
    await client.attach();
    await client.sendText('Hello');
    if (client.error != null) {
      throw StateError(client.error!);
    }
  } finally {
    await subscription.cancel();
    await client.dispose();
  }
}
```
<!-- /example -->

For a direct send on an idle connected client, await `sendText`, then inspect
`client.error` or the snapshot error. Busy-message queue/drop policies may return
before another run completes; observe snapshots for the actual conversation state. Request failures are represented in client state, so
successful completion of the returned future alone does not prove a successful
model response. Invalid API operations can still throw, so keep cleanup in
`finally`.

### Understand ownership

Create a client for the conversation or view that owns it. `attach()` restores
configured history and replay state. Creating a client alone does not join an
existing run. Chat `detach()` is synchronous and releases the attached view;
`dispose()` is asynchronous and ends ownership. Cancel state subscriptions when
their owner no longer needs updates.

`client.snapshot` reads current state. Each listener to `client.states` receives
an initial snapshot, followed by updates. The stream closes on disposal.
Read [chat and rendering](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/seifalmotaz/tanstack-ai-dart/main/doc/chat.md) before modifying message state.

### Add Flutter UI

Use `StreamBuilder<ChatSnapshot>` with `stream: client.states` and
`initialData: client.snapshot`. Create the client outside `build()`, then attach
it when the conversation owner becomes active. Release ownership when the view
is disposed. Flutter's synchronous `State.dispose()` cannot await a future;
arrange asynchronous cleanup through your app's lifecycle or handle the
`client.dispose()` future explicitly.

The package ships a headless client. Message widgets, Markdown rendering,
attachments, and app navigation belong to the consuming application.


## Chat and rendering

Source: [doc/chat.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/seifalmotaz/tanstack-ai-dart/main/doc/chat.md)

## Chat and rendering

Import `package:tanstack_ai_dart/tanstack_ai_dart.dart`. The
[analyzed recipes](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/seifalmotaz/tanstack-ai-dart/main/example/recipes.dart) supply all examples below.

### Read state

Use `client.snapshot`, `client.state`, and `client.isLoading`. `ChatClientState`
contains `submitted`, `streaming`, `ready`, and `error`.
`ChatSnapshot.connectionStatus` uses `ChatConnectionState`, a separate enum.

Listen to `client.states` for updates. Each listener has its own initial snapshot
and pause buffer. Cancelling one listener does not cancel the run or other
listeners. Snapshot errors are data in the state, not stream error events.
A slow paused listener can buffer updates, so cancel unused subscriptions.

`messages` and snapshots are read-only. Use `setMessagesManually(...)` to replace
a transcript; the client copies the input. `getMessages()` is a retained legacy
accessor to live data and should not be used in new UI code.

### Send text or parts

Use `sendText(String)` for text. Typed message input also preserves an explicit
message ID and metadata:

<!-- example: example/recipes.dart#message -->
```dart
Future<void> sendParts(ChatClient client) => client.sendMessage(
      ChatMessageInput.parts(
        [AssistantPart.text('Show properties in Cairo')],
        id: 'customer-message-1',
        metadata: {'language': 'en'},
      ),
    );
```
<!-- /example -->

Unknown wire fields are preserved through conversion. User interface rendering
should use read-only views rather than mutate protocol models.

### Render parts exhaustively

`message.chatParts` and `part.chatPart` produce sealed immutable views. This
switch handles the variants available in the current Dart API:

<!-- example: example/recipes.dart#rendering -->
```dart
String summarizePart(ChatPart part) => switch (part) {
      ChatTextPart(:final content) => content,
      ChatThinkingPart(:final content) => content,
      ChatToolCallPart(:final name) => 'Tool: $name',
      ChatToolResultPart(:final output) => 'Result: $output',
      ChatActivityPart(:final activityType) => 'Activity: $activityType',
      ChatStructuredPart(:final data) => 'Data: $data',
      ChatSubagentPart(:final id) => 'Agent: $id',
      ChatMediaPart(:final mediaType) => 'Media: $mediaType',
      ChatUnknownPart(:final type) => 'Unsupported part: $type',
    };
```
<!-- /example -->

Every view exposes `wire`, the deep-frozen JSON representation. Future protocol
types become `ChatUnknownPart`. Opaque application objects retain their identity;
use immutable models if they are included in outputs.

### Configure busy behavior

The queue can enqueue, drop, or interrupt a message submitted during a run.
Its drain policy supports FIFO or batch behavior. Configure a bounded queue for
your application's workload:

<!-- example: example/recipes.dart#queue -->
```dart
ChatClient queuedChat(ConnectionAdapter connection) => ChatClient(
      connection: connection,
      queue: const ChatQueueConfig(
        whenBusy: QueueWhenBusy.queue,
        maxSize: 10,
        onOverflow: QueueOverflow.reject,
      ),
    );
```
<!-- /example -->

Read `snapshot.queue` to show pending items. The `reject` overflow policy does
not add the new item when the queue is full; a returned send future does not
serve as an explicit enqueue acknowledgement.

### Stop, clear, or replace

- `await client.stop()` cancels the active run, clears queued input, and resets
  pending interrupt state. It is not a storage-preserving pause operation.
- `await client.clear()` clears the conversation and configured stored state.
- `await client.reload()` regenerates from the retained user conversation.
- `client.replaceConnection(next)` replaces the transport and cancels current
  subscription/run ownership. It does not mutate an adapter already in use.

Use typed setters for runtime options: `body`, `forwardedProps`, `context`,
`tools`, `queueConfig`, `byok`, and callbacks. Assign `null` to a nullable option
when you intend to clear it. Read [persistence and resume](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/seifalmotaz/tanstack-ai-dart/main/doc/persistence.md) before
choosing how to leave and later rejoin a conversation.


## Connections and authentication

Source: [doc/connections.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/seifalmotaz/tanstack-ai-dart/main/doc/connections.md)

## Connections and authentication

Import `package:tanstack_ai_dart/tanstack_ai_dart.dart`. All examples below are
extracted from [recipes.dart](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/seifalmotaz/tanstack-ai-dart/main/example/recipes.dart).

### Choose a transport

| Factory | Response format | Application responsibility |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `fetchServerSentEvents` | SSE carrying TanStack chunks | Compatible HTTP backend |
| `fetchHttpStream` | NDJSON chunks or replay envelopes | Compatible HTTP backend |
| `fetchJson` | JSON polling responses | Backend polling contract |
| `xhrServerSentEvents`, `xhrHttpStream` | SSE or NDJSON | Browser XHR when no client is injected |
| `webSocket` | TanStack WebSocket messages | Injected `WebSocketFactory` |
| `stream`, `rpcStream` | Dart streams of decoded chunks | Custom stream implementation |
| `fetcherToConnectionAdapter` | Typed stream or HTTP response | Custom request function |

Fixed URL factories accept a `String` and named `options`. Their corresponding
`...Provider` factories accept async or synchronous URL/options callbacks.
Providers are read for operations that acquire a URL/options pair. See the
adapter source for exact reconnect behavior; do not assume every replayed HTTP
attempt re-runs application callbacks.

### Refresh authentication

Pass token lookup as an argument, so credential ownership stays in your app:

<!-- example: example/recipes.dart#refresh -->
```dart
ChatClient authenticatedChat(
  String endpoint,
  Future<String> Function() readAccessToken,
) =>
    ChatClient(
      connection: fetchServerSentEventsProvider(
        url: () => endpoint,
        options: () async => FetchConnectionOptions(
          headers: {'Authorization': 'Bearer ${await readAccessToken()}'},
        ),
      ),
    );
```
<!-- /example -->

Server authentication, tenant authorization, provider selection, and endpoint
access rules are backend responsibilities. In a browser, cookies and credentialed
requests also depend on CORS and the server's cookie configuration. Configure
`FetchConnectionOptions.credentials` according to your deployment.

Internally created HTTP clients are closed by the adapter. Injected
`package:http` clients stay caller-owned. Cancellation signals are forwarded to
request implementations. A custom fetcher must cooperate with cancellation for
work outside the SDK's stream ownership.

### Supply a custom fetcher

Return `ChatFetcherResult.response` for a `package:http` SSE response or
`ChatFetcherResult.stream` for decoded `Stream<StreamChunk>` values:

<!-- example: example/recipes.dart#fetcher -->
```dart
ChatClient customHttpChat(
  Future<http.StreamedResponse> Function(
    ChatFetcherInput input,
    CancellationSignal? signal,
    Map<String, String>? headers,
  ) request,
) =>
    ChatClient(
      connection: fetcherToConnectionAdapter(
        (input, {signal, headers}) async => ChatFetcherResult.response(
          await request(input, signal, headers),
        ),
      ),
    );
```
<!-- /example -->

`request` is an application-provided function. The explicit result variant
replaces a runtime union of unrelated return types.

Custom adapters use either `ConnectionAdapter.connect(connect: ...)` or
`ConnectionAdapter.subscription(subscribe: ..., send: ...)`. Required parameters
prevent partial or mixed modes during analysis. Add `hydrate` and `joinRun`
handlers when your backend supports durable history and live replay.

### Match the backend protocol

The HTTP streaming adapter sends JSON run-agent input, including messages and
run context, to your endpoint. SSE responses carry TanStack event chunks and
must have the expected streaming body. Durable replay additionally depends on
the server's run IDs and event offsets. A generic OpenAI-compatible text stream
is not interchangeable with this protocol.

The supported source revision is listed in the [README](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/seifalmotaz/tanstack-ai-dart/main/README.md).
Read [parity methodology](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/seifalmotaz/tanstack-ai-dart/main/PARITY.md) and the
pinned official source linked by the README compatibility table
when implementing or changing a backend contract.


## Persistence and resume

Source: [doc/persistence.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/seifalmotaz/tanstack-ai-dart/main/doc/persistence.md)

## Persistence and resume

Choose a stable conversation ID before enabling persistence. User IDs alone are
usually insufficient when a user can own multiple conversations. Keep tenant
isolation and storage access control in your application and backend.

Import `package:tanstack_ai_dart/tanstack_ai_dart.dart` for these recipes.

### Use server-authoritative history

The server option uses the connection's hydration and join-run handlers. History
paging is configured on that persistence choice:

<!-- example: example/recipes.dart#server-persistence -->
```dart
ChatClient serverHistory(ConnectionAdapter connection, String threadId) =>
    ChatClient(
      connection: connection,
      persistence: ChatPersistenceOptions.server(
        threadId: threadId,
        history: const ChatHistoryConfig(pageSize: 20),
      ),
    );
```
<!-- /example -->

Call `await client.attach()` after construction. Read `hasOlderMessages` and call
`await client.loadOlderMessages()` to fetch earlier pages. Backend handlers must
support the paging contract; changing page size cannot add server capabilities.

### Store messages in your application

Provide an adapter that stores the complete chat record:

<!-- example: example/recipes.dart#stored-persistence -->
```dart
ChatClient storedHistory(
  ConnectionAdapter connection,
  ChatClientPersistence storage,
  String threadId,
) =>
    ChatClient(
      connection: connection,
      persistence: ChatPersistenceOptions.stored(
        threadId: threadId,
        adapter: storage,
      ),
    );
```
<!-- /example -->

`ChatClientPersistence` defines `getItem(id)`, `setItem(id, ChatPersistedState)`,
and `removeItem(id)`. Methods may be synchronous or asynchronous. Store the
messages and resume snapshot as one record, using `state.toJson()` and
`ChatPersistedState.fromJson(...)` at your serialization boundary.
`ChatStorageAdapter` offers a typed read result for new implementations.

The SDK does not install a device database, browser store, or secure-storage
plugin. Inject the application's storage implementation. A memory-only adapter
cannot preserve a conversation across process restarts.

### Rejoin a live run

A resume pointer identifies the prior thread and run. `ChatResumeSnapshot` also
carries pending interrupts. Pass restored state through configured storage or
`initialResumeSnapshot`, then attach the client. The connection and backend must
provide replay support.

Hydrated pending interrupts and replay failures have explicit client handling.
A quiet connection does not prove that a run is dead. Do not erase a resume
pointer merely because no new tokens have arrived.

`stop()` intentionally cancels and resets pending run state. Use the lifecycle
operations described in [chat and rendering](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/seifalmotaz/tanstack-ai-dart/main/doc/chat.md) when leaving a view.
`clear()` also removes configured client storage; provide an explicit application
confirmation if losing that conversation would surprise the user.


## Tools and interrupts

Source: [doc/tools-and-interrupts.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/seifalmotaz/tanstack-ai-dart/main/doc/tools-and-interrupts.md)

## Tools and interrupts

Tools run application code on the client. Define the input, output, validation,
and approval policy deliberately. The SDK does not grant access to operating
system or business actions on its own.

Import `package:tanstack_ai_dart/tanstack_ai_dart.dart` for the examples below.

### Define a typed tool

Use `ClientTool<TInput, TOutput>` in an ordinary Dart list. A validating schema
can decode raw wire values into an application model before execution:

<!-- example: example/recipes.dart#tool -->
```dart
ClientTool<String, int> lengthTool() => ClientTool<String, int>(
      name: 'length',
      description: 'Count characters in text',
      inputSchema: StandardSchema(
        (value) => value is String
            ? SchemaValidationResult.success(value)
            : const SchemaValidationResult.failure(
                [SchemaIssue('Expected text')],
              ),
        schema: {'type': 'string'},
      ),
      execute: (text, context) => text.length,
    );
```
<!-- /example -->

Register it with `client.tools = [lengthTool()]`, or pass the list to the chat
constructor. Execution callbacks return `FutureOr<TOutput>` and receive a
`ToolCallContext` containing caller context and cancellation.

`RawJsonSchema` describes a schema but does not validate inputs. Use
`StandardSchema` when validation or decoding is required. Output schemas can
validate the returned value as well. The Dart type arguments describe the
callback contract; they do not derive a runtime validator from a Dart class.

### Request approval

Set `needsApproval: true` on a tool whose execution requires the user's choice.
Render pending approvals from the client's interrupt/tool state. When the user
answers a known approval ID:

<!-- example: example/recipes.dart#approval -->
```dart
Future<void> answerApproval(
  ChatClient client,
  String approvalId,
  bool approved,
) =>
    client.addToolApprovalResponse(id: approvalId, approved: approved);
```
<!-- /example -->

Approval response submission and automatic continuation use the active run
context. Do not submit a normal message while a blocking interrupt is pending.
The client rejects that operation so the interrupted run is not bypassed.

For manually executed tools, use `addToolResult(toolCallId: ..., output: ...)`
with the ID supplied by the active tool call. Preserve explicit `null` outputs;
missing output and an output whose value is `null` are different protocol states.

### Handle generic interrupts

`ChatInterruptDefinition` registers an interrupt and optional schemas/validation.
Inspect `client.getInterruptState()` or `snapshot.interruptState` for pending
items. `resolveInterrupts`, `cancelInterrupts`, and `retryInterrupts` operate on
managed pending definitions. `resumeInterrupts` accepts serialized resolution
entries for the active interrupted context.

Keep the server's interrupt IDs and response shape intact. Low-level unsafe
resume operations require explicit durable IDs and should be reserved for an
integration that owns those IDs. Never infer an approval from the language
model's text response.

### Keep application context typed at the boundary

Caller context is `Object?` because one client may register heterogeneous tools.
Validate or cast it to your own model before using it. Dart does not reproduce
TypeScript intersections of every registered tool's context requirements.
See [API compatibility](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/seifalmotaz/tanstack-ai-dart/main/API_COMPATIBILITY.md) for other language adaptations.


## Generation and video

Source: [doc/generation.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/seifalmotaz/tanstack-ai-dart/main/doc/generation.md)

## Generation and video

Import `package:tanstack_ai_dart/tanstack_ai_dart.dart`. Use the default
`GenerationClient` constructor with a connection, or `.fetcher` for a typed
application request. Video uses `VideoGenerationClient`.

### Return a typed result

The three `GenerationClient<TInput, TResult, TOutput>` parameters represent the
request, raw result, and published output. They can be the same result type when
no transformation is needed:

<!-- example: example/recipes.dart#generation -->
```dart
Future<String?> generateText(
  Future<String> Function(String prompt, CancellationSignal signal) request,
  String prompt,
) async {
  final generator = GenerationClient<String, String, String>.fetcher(
    fetcher: (input, options) async => GenerationFetchResult.value(
      await request(input, options.signal),
    ),
  );
  try {
    await generator.generate(prompt);
    if (generator.error != null) throw generator.error!;
    return generator.result;
  } finally {
    generator.dispose();
  }
}
```
<!-- /example -->

The `request` function belongs to the application. It receives the SDK's
cancellation signal. `GenerationFetchResult.value(...)` wraps a result;
`.stream(...)` wraps decoded TanStack chunks; `.response(...)` wraps a
`package:http` streaming response. These variants keep transport responses
separate from application data.

`generate()` reports request failures through `error` and the state stream.
Check the error after awaiting it. `snapshot`, `states`, `state`, `result`, and
`isLoading` provide the current lifecycle. Generation client `stop()` and
`dispose()` are synchronous; chat's corresponding methods return futures.

### Generate video

The video fetcher receives `VideoGenerateInput` and returns a `VideoGenerateResult`:

<!-- example: example/recipes.dart#video -->
```dart
VideoGenerationClient<VideoGenerateResult> videoClient(
  Future<VideoGenerateResult> Function(
    VideoGenerateInput input,
    GenerationFetcherOptions options,
  ) request,
) =>
    VideoGenerationClient<VideoGenerateResult>.fetcher(
      fetcher: (input, options) async => GenerationFetchResult.value(
        await request(input, options),
      ),
    );
```
<!-- /example -->

Call `generate(VideoGenerateInput(...))` on the returned client, then inspect
`jobId`, `videoStatus`, and result state. The backend owns provider jobs and
artifact serving; the SDK does not create a video-provider service.

### Transform and restore

`onResult` can return a `GenerationTransformOutcome<TOutput>` to publish a
transformed result or preserve the prior value. `reconstructResult` handles
server-restored artifact records. Media-specific reconstruction helpers include
`reconstructImageResult`, `reconstructAudioResult`, and
`reconstructTranscriptionResult`.

Use `GenerationPersistenceOptions.persistent(threadId: ...)` for server-driven
persistence. The thread ID must stay stable across reloads, and the connection
must implement compatible generation hydration and replay. The default is
`.ephemeral(...)`.

### Preserve snapshot ownership

JSON maps/lists and scalar-typed JSON collections are copied read-only for
publication. The `result` getter retains the original result. Status changes
preserve the published result identity when that result has not changed.
Opaque class instances retain identity; use immutable models.

Other reified collection shapes need an explicit `copySnapshotResult` callback.
For a result such as `Map<String, List<int>>`, use this function:

<!-- example: example/recipes.dart#copier -->
```dart
Map<String, List<int>> copyScores(Map<String, List<int>> value) =>
    Map<String, List<int>>.unmodifiable({
      for (final entry in value.entries)
        entry.key: List<int>.unmodifiable(entry.value),
    });
```
<!-- /example -->

A missing compatible copier produces `SnapshotCopyException` in client error
state. A supplied copier must isolate its result and freeze nested mutable data.


## Platform support

Source: [doc/platform-support.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/seifalmotaz/tanstack-ai-dart/main/doc/platform-support.md)

## Platform support and application responsibilities

The core SDK uses Dart and has no Flutter dependency. Platform-specific features
are injected interfaces rather than bundled Flutter plugins.

| Feature | SDK responsibility | Application responsibility |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Chat, queues, interrupts, and generation | State and protocol processing | Endpoint, credentials, rendering |
| HTTP streaming | SSE, NDJSON, polling, cancellation | Backend and browser CORS policy |
| WebSocket | Run/message handling and reconnection | `WebSocketFactory` implementation |
| Conversation storage | Storage record and lifecycle contracts | Browser or device store implementation |
| Audio recording | Recorder interface and output conversion | Microphone permissions and media host |
| Realtime sessions | Session state and event handling | Realtime connection and media host |
| BYOK | Keyring contracts, headers, and crypto | Key-entry UI, storage, server policy |
| Passkeys | Keyring cryptography and host interface | WebAuthn ceremony and credential storage |
| MCP and WebMCP | Tool/bridge interfaces | Actual host messaging and registration |
| Devtools | Bridge contracts and snapshots | Panel or host integration |

[Validation evidence](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/seifalmotaz/tanstack-ai-dart/main/VALIDATION.md) distinguishes controlled-host tests from
real hardware verification. Missing host support is reported as unavailable or
unsupported by the relevant capability. An interface existing in the package
does not mean a device integration is installed.

### Use the SDK from Flutter

Create a chat client outside widget `build()`. Bind its `states` stream to a
`StreamBuilder<ChatSnapshot>` or the app's existing state-management system.
Use `client.snapshot` for the initial UI. Attach when its owner becomes active,
and release subscriptions and the client when ownership ends.

Flutter `State.dispose()` is synchronous. Handle chat's asynchronous cleanup
through your app's lifecycle rather than declaring an async override. Generation
and video disposal are synchronous. The package provides no UI widgets,
authentication screens, navigation, or permission dialogs.

### Choose credentials and BYOK deliberately

Ordinary backend authentication belongs in connection headers or an options
provider. Read [connections and authentication](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/seifalmotaz/tanstack-ai-dart/main/doc/connections.md).

For bring-your-own-key integrations, `defineByok` creates a keyring client.
Pass that client through the chat/generation `byok` option and select a provider
with `byokProvider` when needed. Prepared provider keys are forwarded in BYOK
headers for the active operation, not inserted into message text or JSON bodies.
The backend must understand those headers and enforce its own provider policy.

Memory key storage is not durable secure device storage. Supply the required
storage/passkey host for persistence and show the SDK's missing/locked prompt
state in your UI. Never put real keys in examples, issue reports, or application
logs. No provider account or endpoint is bundled with this package.

### Review the public libraries

Use the [API reference map](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/seifalmotaz/tanstack-ai-dart/main/doc/api-reference.md) to choose an import. Domain imports
can keep application dependencies explicit. Browser storage names do not imply
that `dart:io` implements browser APIs, and XHR factory names do not imply an
`XMLHttpRequest` instance exists on native platforms.


## API reference map

Source: [doc/api-reference.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/seifalmotaz/tanstack-ai-dart/main/doc/api-reference.md)

## API reference map

The main import is `package:tanstack_ai_dart/tanstack_ai_dart.dart`. This page
maps tasks to public Dart symbols. It is not a generated declaration reference.
Generate local API documentation with `dart doc`; open `doc/api/index.html`.
A hosted pub.dev API URL will be added after an actual package release.

### Choose a public library

| Import suffix | Main purpose | Entry points |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `tanstack_ai_dart.dart` | Common application entry point | Chat, generation, connections, platform contracts |
| `chat.dart` | Chat state and orchestration | `ChatClient`, `ChatSnapshot`, `ChatMessageInput`, queue and persistence options |
| `connections.dart` | Transports and run context | `ConnectionAdapter`, HTTP/provider factories, `ChatFetcherResult`, cancellation |
| `generation.dart` | Generation and video | `GenerationClient`, `VideoGenerationClient`, `GenerationFetchResult`, restoration helpers |
| `ui.dart` | Typed rendering selectors | Sealed `ChatPart` views and typed tool/result selectors |
| `byok.dart` | Bring-your-own-key support | `defineByok`, storage/provider contracts, keyring errors |
| `platform.dart` | Host implementations | Audio, realtime, storage, MCP, WebMCP, schema interfaces |
| `processing.dart` | Low-level message processing | `StreamProcessor`, chunk conversion, partial JSON strategies |
| `devtools.dart` | Debugging bridges | Devtools clients, ports, and bridge factories |

Avoid imports from `lib/src`. Public libraries define the supported import paths.
Some imports expose matching hydration names with different message models.
Qualify domain imports when using both chat and wire-level hydration together.

### Common chat operations

| Task | API |
| --- | --- |
| Read state | `snapshot`, `state`, `isLoading`, `messages` |
| Observe state | `states.listen(...)` |
| Restore configured state | `await attach()` |
| Release an attached view | `detach()` |
| End client ownership | `await dispose()` |
| Send text | `await sendText(...)` |
| Send typed parts/metadata | `await sendMessage(ChatMessageInput.parts(...))` |
| Stop current work | `await stop()` |
| Clear conversation and configured storage | `await clear()` |
| Page history | `hasOlderMessages`, `await loadOlderMessages()` |
| Replace transcript | `setMessagesManually(...)` |
| Replace transport | `replaceConnection(...)` |
| Respond to tool approval | `await addToolApprovalResponse(...)` |
| Submit a manual tool result | `await addToolResult(...)` |
| Resolve managed interrupts | `resolveInterrupts(...)`, `cancelInterrupts()`, `retryInterrupts()` |

### Common generation operations

Construct a connected client or use `.fetcher(...)`. Read `snapshot`, `states`,
`state`, `result`, and `error`. Await `generate(input)`. Call synchronous `stop()`
or `dispose()` for cancellation or cleanup. Video adds `jobId` and `videoStatus`.

### Configuration contracts

Use typed options rather than JavaScript-style unions. `ToolSchema` values are
explicit validators or raw schema descriptors. `ClientTool<TInput, TOutput>`
keeps callback types, while wire values remain extensible JSON maps.

The [compatibility inventory](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/seifalmotaz/tanstack-ai-dart/main/tool/upstream_api_compatibility.json) records
upstream exports, their Dart representation, and language/platform adaptations.
[API compatibility](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/seifalmotaz/tanstack-ai-dart/main/API_COMPATIBILITY.md) explains the decisions.
Legacy constructors/accessors are compatibility paths described in
[MIGRATION.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/seifalmotaz/tanstack-ai-dart/main/MIGRATION.md).


## Troubleshooting

Source: [doc/troubleshooting.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/seifalmotaz/tanstack-ai-dart/main/doc/troubleshooting.md)

## Troubleshooting

### The endpoint returns text but no assistant message

Confirm that the endpoint implements the supported TanStack client protocol.
A provider's raw token stream or an arbitrary JSON response is not a TanStack
chunk stream. Check the response status, streaming content type, terminal events,
and the transport factory. See [connections](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/seifalmotaz/tanstack-ai-dart/main/doc/connections.md).

### Awaiting send succeeds but the run has an error

Inspect `client.error` and `snapshot.error`. Network/model failures are represented
in state, so completion of the send future alone is not a success signal.
Configuration errors and invalid operations can throw. Keep cleanup in `finally`.

### Authentication works natively but fails in a browser

Review server CORS rules, cookies, credential mode, and allowed request headers.
Do not send a real bearer token in a bug report. The SDK cannot grant cross-origin
access that the server refuses. Use provider options for refreshed credentials.

### History or replay does not restore

Check the stable thread ID, persistence mode, and backend hydration/join support.
Construction alone does not restore history; call `attach()`. A memory store
cannot survive an application restart. Read [persistence](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/seifalmotaz/tanstack-ai-dart/main/doc/persistence.md).

### Sending is blocked by an interrupt

Resolve or cancel the actual pending approval/interrupt before sending a normal
message. Keep the original interrupt IDs and run context. Read
[tools and interrupts](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/seifalmotaz/tanstack-ai-dart/main/doc/tools-and-interrupts.md).

### A mutation throws UnsupportedError

Published state and typed part views are read-only. Use explicit client actions,
such as `setMessagesManually(...)`, instead of editing a snapshot. Copy data into
an application-owned model if it needs independent editing.

### Generation reports SnapshotCopyException

The output collection type cannot be copied without losing its reified Dart type.
Supply `copySnapshotResult` for that shape, including nested mutable collections.
The [generation guide](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/seifalmotaz/tanstack-ai-dart/main/doc/generation.md) includes a typed copier example.

### The compiler rejects an old example

Check that the example targets the Dart 0.3 API. Use named options, typed fetcher
results, and required connection modes. Read [MIGRATION.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/seifalmotaz/tanstack-ai-dart/main/MIGRATION.md).
Do not paste a TypeScript example directly into Dart.

### A platform capability is unavailable

Supply the required host implementation and permissions. Package interfaces and
mock-host tests do not install a microphone, WebAuthn service, socket, database,
or MCP host. See [platform support](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/seifalmotaz/tanstack-ai-dart/main/doc/platform-support.md).

### Report a remaining problem

Open a [GitHub issue](https://github.com/seifalmotaz/tanstack-ai-dart/issues) with
the Dart/package versions, platform, transport, sanitized stack trace, and a
minimal reproduction. State whether it reproduces against the pinned official
client. Keep private data, credentials, and production account access out of the
report.


## Migration to 0.3

Source: [MIGRATION.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/seifalmotaz/tanstack-ai-dart/main/MIGRATION.md)

## Migrating to 0.3

The wire protocol and TanStack client behavior remain pinned to the same upstream
commit. The default Dart API changes before the first pub.dev publication.

| Previous usage | Dart API |
| --- | --- |
| `ChatClient(options: ChatClientOptions(...))` | `ChatClient(connection: ..., namedParameter: ...)` |
| `fetchServerSentEvents(url, options)` | `fetchServerSentEvents(url, options: options)` |
| URL/options as either values or callbacks | Static factory or named `...Provider(url: callback, options: callback)` |
| Optional connect/subscribe/send fields | `ConnectionAdapter.connect(...)` or `.subscription(...)` |
| Fetcher returns arbitrary `Object` | `ChatFetcherResult.stream(...)` or `.response(...)` |
| Generation fetcher returns arbitrary `Object` | `GenerationClient.fetcher` and `GenerationFetchResult.value/stream/response` |
| `subscribeSnapshot` plus unsubscribe callback | `states.listen(...)` and `StreamSubscription.cancel()` |
| `getSnapshot()`, `getState()`, `getIsLoading()` | `snapshot`, `state`, `isLoading` |
| Chat status strings | `ChatClientState` and `ChatConnectionState` enums |
| `sendMessage` accepts text/map/parts | `sendText(String)` or `sendMessage(ChatMessageInput.text/parts(...))` |
| Boolean/storage persistence union | `ChatPersistenceOptions.ephemeral/server/stored` |
| Generation boolean persistence | `GenerationPersistenceOptions.ephemeral/persistent` |
| Mutable `client.messages` | Read-only transcript; use `setMessagesManually(...)` |
| `updateOptions` with untyped optional values | Typed setters; assigning `null` explicitly clears nullable configuration |
| Raw input/output schema passed to a tool | `RawJsonSchema(...)` or a validating `StandardSchema(...)` |
| `clientTools([...])` | A normal Dart list |
| Approval schema reflection/side table | `tool.approvalSchema` field |
| String-discriminated mutable parts for rendering | Sealed immutable `message.chatParts` / `part.chatPart` views |

`ChatClient.status` and `ChatSnapshot.status` expose `ChatClientState`; the legacy
`getStatus()` method still returns the wire string. `ChatSnapshot.connectionStatus`
is a `ChatConnectionState`. Serialize enum `.name` when a wire string is needed.

Use `ChatClient.legacy(...)` for previous constructor options/aliases and raw
fetcher unions. Use `sendLegacyMessage(...)` and `updateLegacyOptions(...)` only
while migrating older JS-shaped call sites. Their behavior remains tested against
the pinned upstream suite. Legacy `getMessages()` intentionally retains its live
mutable-list contract; the default transcript/snapshot getters are read-only.

The three generation type parameters distinguish input, raw result, and transformed
output. They remain explicit where needed; schema-driven TypeScript inference is
not reproduced. Typed fetchers distinguish results from transport responses even
when an application result itself happens to be a response/stream-like object.

For Flutter, subscribe using `StreamBuilder` or the app's existing state management.
The core package has no Flutter dependency. State streams emit an initial snapshot
per listener, then updates, and close when their owner is disposed.


## API compatibility

Source: [API_COMPATIBILITY.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/seifalmotaz/tanstack-ai-dart/main/API_COMPATIBILITY.md)

## Upstream API compatibility

### Dart API revision 0.3

The default API uses typed named parameters, enum state, replaying state streams,
sealed fetcher results and read-only consumer message views. JavaScript-shaped
constructors and getter/callback aliases are explicit compatibility paths rather
than the recommended usage. See [MIGRATION.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/seifalmotaz/tanstack-ai-dart/main/MIGRATION.md).

All pinned upstream runtime exports remain reachable for compatibility. Two
upstream runtime-invalid connection configuration cases are now verified by
analyzer-negative fixtures: Dart constructors make those states unrepresentable.
The wire protocol and valid run behavior are unchanged.


This reference records the reviewed public exports and the Dart-specific type
contract. Test results and supported toolchains are in [VALIDATION.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/seifalmotaz/tanstack-ai-dart/main/VALIDATION.md).

Target: `@tanstack/ai-client` 0.40.0 and `@tanstack/ai` 0.70.0, commit
`7095ebbf1b59175f0cd339c1c477d6af55b312de`. Pinned upstream source:
[ai-client source](https://github.com/TanStack/ai/tree/7095ebbf1b59175f0cd339c1c477d6af55b312de/packages/ai-client/src).

The machine-readable inventory is
[`tool/upstream_api_compatibility.json`](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/seifalmotaz/tanstack-ai-dart/main/tool/upstream_api_compatibility.json).
The executable inventory check is
[`test/interop/public_export_inventory_test.dart`](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/seifalmotaz/tanstack-ai-dart/main/test/interop/public_export_inventory_test.dart).

### Method

Every export listed in `tool/upstream_api.json` was reviewed: 185 root, 21 BYOK
and 41 UI, for 247 total. For each export this audit:

1. Resolved the corresponding public barrel recursively, honoring every
   `export ... show` and `export ... hide` directive:
   - root (`index`): `lib/tanstack_ai_dart.dart`
   - BYOK: `lib/byok.dart`
   - UI: `lib/ui.dart`
2. Located the actual Dart declaration or runtime implementation in `lib/`, not
   merely a matching substring or a similarly named file.
3. Distinguished runtime exports from type-only exports and checked that every
   runtime export is reachable and usable from its public barrel.
4. Recorded either a concrete Dart equivalent or a concrete TypeScript-only,
   platform, or server-out-of-scope reason.

`dart-equivalent` in the JSON means "a public Dart symbol exists and is usable
from the corresponding barrel"; it does not by itself claim behavioral parity.
Behavioral coverage remains tracked by the separate upstream-test mapping audit.

### Counts

| Surface | Upstream barrel | Runtime | Type | Total | Dart equivalent | Dart adapted | Platform interface | Language limitation | Server out of scope | Name collision |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| `index` | `lib/tanstack_ai_dart.dart` | 50 | 135 | 185 | 77 | 85 | 7 | 15 | 0 | 1 |
| `byok` | `lib/byok.dart` | 11 | 10 | 21 | 17 | 0 | 3 | 0 | 1 | 0 |
| `ui` | `lib/ui.dart` | 6 | 35 | 41 | 13 | 8 | 0 | 20 | 0 | 0 |
| **Total** | | **67** | **180** | **247** | **107** | **93** | **10** | **35** | **1** | **1** |

Status meanings:

- `dart-equivalent`: same-name public Dart symbol with the same role.
- `dart-adapted`: public Dart symbol exists but the contract differs in shape
  (renamed, collapsed union, explicit generic, or literal union replaced by
  `String`/an enum).
- `platform-interface`: public runtime symbol exists, but the capability needs
  an injected host implementation and reports unavailable without one.
- `language-limitation`: TypeScript conditional, mapped, literal-union, tuple or
  utility type with no direct Dart type; the JSON records the Dart workaround
  when one exists.
- `server-out-of-scope`: export belongs to the `@tanstack/ai` server/provider
  package, not this client SDK.
- `name-collision`: an exported Dart name exists but has a different contract
  from the upstream export.

No upstream runtime export is missing from the three public barrels: 67/67
runtime exports are reachable. The JSON still records 35 language limitations
and 1 documented legacy name collision.

### Runtime exports

All 67 runtime exports are referenced by the inventory test and are usable from
their public barrel. This includes the 50 root exports, 11 BYOK exports and 6 UI
selectors.

Ten of them are marked `platform-interface` because they require a host seam:

- `AudioRecorder` requires an `AudioRecorderPlatform` backed by browser media
  APIs.
- `getWebMCPTools`, `registerWebMCPTools`, `subscribeWebMCPTools` require a
  WebMCP host context.
- `localStoragePersistence`, `sessionStoragePersistence`,
  `indexedDBPersistence` require browser storage and raise
  `StorageUnavailableError` otherwise.
- `defaultByokStorage`, `isPasskeyStorageSupported`, `passkeyStorage` require a
  WebAuthn/passkey host; the keyring HKDF/AES-GCM cryptography itself is real
  Dart.

The remaining runtime exports are ordinary Dart implementations. `clientTools`
was confirmed directly in `lib/src/platform/tool_types.dart:184` and through the
root export chain; it is public despite being missed by a naive declaration
scan.

### Type contract

The Dart port intentionally does not emulate TypeScript's type system. The
current contract is:

- **Caller context is `Object?`.** `ChatClientOptions.context`,
  `ToolCallContext.context`, WebMCP options and strategy inputs carry `Object?`.
  Context requirements are not inferred from registered tools or schemas.
  Callers must cast or validate it themselves.
- **Inputs and outputs are explicit generics.** `ClientTool<TInput, TOutput>`,
  `GenerationClient<TInput, TResult, TOutput>` and
  `VideoGenerationClient<TOutput>` support explicit types and ordinary Dart
  callback inference. There is no schema-to-type inference.
- **No heterogeneous tuple, literal, conditional or mapped inference.** The
  upstream `Infer*`, `Extract*`, `ChatUI*Of`, `DistributedOmit` and similar
  helpers have no Dart equivalent. `clientTools` returns a list, not a tuple;
  tool names are `String`, not literal unions.
- **Literal unions become `String` or enums.** Examples: `ConnectionStatus` and
  `PersistedArtifactRole` are `String`; `WhenBusy` is `QueueWhenBusy`;
  `InterruptItemStatus` is `ChatInterruptStatus`.
- **Unions become one concrete class.** `UIMessage` maps to `AssistantTurn`;
  every message part maps to `AssistantPart` discriminated by `type`;
  interrupt variants map to `ChatInterrupt` discriminated by `kind`.
- **UI selectors are concrete, with explicit typed helpers.** `ui.dart` exposes
  concrete selected-part classes. `typed_ui.dart` adds explicit
  `ChatTyped*` helpers for callers that want tool input/output typing without
  pretending Dart inferred it.

These are documented as adaptations, not as parity with TypeScript's
compile-time inference. Runtime presence is not a substitute for a type-level
guarantee.

### Notable adaptations

- `UIMessage` / `MessagePart` / part interfaces -> `AssistantTurn` /
  `AssistantPart`.
- `ChatClientSnapshot` -> `ChatSnapshot`; `ConnectionStatus` -> `String`.
- `ChatPendingInterrupt` and the bound/generic/approval interrupt unions ->
  `ChatInterrupt`; `InterruptItemStatus` -> `ChatInterruptStatus`.
- `WhenBusy` -> `QueueWhenBusy`; `QueueConfig` -> `ChatQueueConfig`;
  `SendMessageOptions` -> `ChatSendOptions`.
- `MultimodalContent` -> `ChatMessageInput`; `ChatRequestBody` ->
  `Map<String, dynamic>`.
- `AudioGenerateInput`, `SpeechGenerateInput`,
  `TranscriptionGenerateInput` and `SummarizeGenerateInput` have no named Dart
  model. `GenerationClient<TInput, TResult, TOutput>` accepts a `Map<String, dynamic>` with the
  documented wire fields or any object exposing `toJson()`.
- `WebMCP*` type names map to Dart `WebMcp*`; runtime function names keep the
  upstream `WebMCP` spelling.
- `ChatFetcherOptions` is represented by named `signal`/`headers` parameters on
  the `ChatFetcher` typedef.

### Name collision

`ChatTransport` is the one exported name whose Dart contract is not the
upstream contract. Upstream `ChatTransport` is the 0.40 XOR union of
`{ connection }` or `{ fetcher }`. The exported Dart `ChatTransport` is the
legacy 0.42-era stream transport. The 0.40 contract is represented by
`ChatClient(connection: ...)`, typed fetcher adapters, and
`ConnectionAdapter`. Do not treat the Dart `ChatTransport` symbol as the
upstream 0.40 union; see the gaps file.

### Server and platform scope

`ByokProviderInit` comes from the `@tanstack/ai/byok` server package and is
outside this client port. Provider/model adapters and server orchestration from
`@tanstack/ai` are likewise out of scope. This package is a client SDK, not a
provider/server adapter and not a Flutter hardware plugin.

### Verification

Check the public export references:

```sh
dart analyze test/interop/public_export_inventory_test.dart
dart test test/interop/public_export_inventory_test.dart
```

The test references every runtime export from the public barrels, every
same-name type export, and the principal adapted types. It also exercises
representative runtime behavior (`partTypeToKey`, `collectInlineToolNames`,
`parsePartialJSON`, `generateMessageId`, `clientTools`, `defineByok`,
`memoryStorage`, `defineByokProvider`, and UI selection).

### Compatibility decisions

`ChatTransport` keeps its existing legacy stream-transport meaning for callers
using the 0.42 protocol. Use `ChatClient(connection: ...)` for the default Dart API.
`ChatClientOptions` is only for `ChatClient.legacy`; custom fetchers become typed
connection adapters through `fetcherToConnectionAdapter`. The constructor rejects conflicting connection and
fetcher options at runtime. No alias claims to provide the TypeScript XOR type.

Caller context remains `Object?` by design. A consuming application should
validate it as its own model before using it. Adding wrapper clients would not
provide TypeScript's automatic intersection of heterogeneous tool contexts.

Generation snapshots copy JSON containers and JSON scalar collections read-only.
Other reified collection shapes use `copySnapshotResult`; see the example and
migration note in [README.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/seifalmotaz/tanstack-ai-dart/main/README.md). Opaque class instances retain identity,
so their mutability is the responsibility of their model implementation.

Host-dependent capabilities require implementations supplied by the consuming
application, including a WebSocket factory for WebSocket connections.
This package does not claim to implement a Flutter audio,
WebAuthn, native-storage, or MCP host plugin.


## Parity methodology

Source: [PARITY.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/seifalmotaz/tanstack-ai-dart/main/PARITY.md)

## Compatibility and verification

Target: `@tanstack/ai-client` 0.40.0, `@tanstack/ai` 0.70.0.
Upstream commit: `7095ebbf1b59175f0cd339c1c477d6af55b312de`.
Source: <https://github.com/TanStack/ai> (MIT; see THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES).

The pinned JavaScript client suite was executed locally: **1,011 Vitest cases
passed**, with no skipped or failed cases. Its TypeScript compilation also
passed. Of those Vitest registrations, 45 exercise TypeScript types rather
than runtime behavior. The `.test-d.ts` fixtures add further compile assertions;
they are tracked separately from executable Dart cases. Exact conditional type
inference is not claimed where Dart has no corresponding language feature.
`tool/upstream_tests.json` records the exact cases and
`tool/upstream_api.json` records exports. These manifests are the comparison
baseline, not a claim that all Dart behavior already matches.

Executed validation: [VALIDATION.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/seifalmotaz/tanstack-ai-dart/main/VALIDATION.md).
Release/integration checklist: [NEXT_STEPS.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/seifalmotaz/tanstack-ai-dart/main/NEXT_STEPS.md).

### Verification commands

Run from the package directory:

```sh
dart pub get
dart analyze
dart test --reporter json > .dart_tool/tests.jsonl
dart run tool/verify_types.dart
dart run tool/parity_audit.dart .dart_tool/tests.jsonl .dart_tool/parity.json
dart test --platform chrome
dart run tool/verify_browser.dart
dart pub publish --dry-run
```

`verify_browser.dart` starts a temporary local HTTP server and tests actual
cross-origin XHR cookies, Arabic content, and cancellation in Chrome. It closes
the server afterward. Chrome must be installed. It does not contact production.
The ordinary transport tests also run in the Dart VM and with injected HTTP
clients, including cancellation before headers and durable stream replay.

`verify_types.dart` invokes the Dart analyzer on positive fixtures and checks
negative fixtures against `expect-error` markers. Those intentionally invalid
fixtures are excluded from ordinary package analysis. Dart generics and runtime
validation replace TypeScript conditional/mapped types where no literal Dart
translation exists. A runtime `runtimeType` equality is not a type-level check.

The parity audit consumes explicit per-case mappings and checks that the named
Dart test actually ran and passed. A title-only match remains an uncovered
review candidate. The mappings record the assertion review and any Dart
adaptation. Invalid JS connection unions are now checked by actual analyzer
fixtures because typed Dart constructors cannot represent those configurations. Extra fixture cases, generated parser
prefixes, or repeated platform runs cannot substitute for missing upstream
behavior. Module mappings and actual test results should be considered together.

See [MIGRATION.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/seifalmotaz/tanstack-ai-dart/main/MIGRATION.md) for the Dart-native API revision. Existing
JS-shaped signatures are explicit legacy paths, not the default Dart usage.

### Platform boundaries

The Dart SDK includes HTTP/SSE/NDJSON, websocket adapters, message processing,
chat/queue/history/interrupt logic, generation/video orchestration, persistence
contracts, BYOK, tool schemas, and devtools bridges. Server orchestration and
provider/model adapters from `@tanstack/ai` are outside the client-port scope.

Browser-only host capabilities (microphone/media recording, WebAuthn ceremonies,
MCP host messaging, WebMCP registration, browser storage) use explicit injected
platform interfaces. They require a platform implementation in the consuming
application. Missing hardware or host support reports unavailable; tests use
controlled host implementations. Passkey keyring cryptography itself is real
HKDF-SHA256/AES-GCM and is checked against a WebCrypto vector.

JavaScript `Response` is represented by `package:http`'s `StreamedResponse`;
`AsyncIterable` by Dart `Stream`. Extensible wire messages remain JSON maps.
Typed `AssistantTurn`/`AssistantPart` models preserve unknown wire fields.
The legacy transport remains a separate compatibility path for 0.42-era servers.

No package publication is implied by local test success or a publish dry run.


## Validation evidence

Source: [VALIDATION.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/seifalmotaz/tanstack-ai-dart/main/VALIDATION.md)

## Validation

Dart API revision 0.3.0 validated on 2026-11-03 on macOS arm64.
The counts below record that API validation snapshot; subsequent documentation
checks and examples are verified separately by CI. The official
TanStack client baseline remains pinned; no CRM credentials or production calls
are needed for these checks.

| Check | Dart 3.13.3 | Minimum Dart 3.6.2 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Full VM suite | 2,457 passed; no failures or skips | 2,457 passed; no failures or skips |
| Full Chrome suite | 1,722 passed; no failures or skips | Not repeated for API revision 0.3 |
| Static rejection assertions | 56 checked; positive fixtures clean | 56 checked; positive fixtures clean |
| Package analysis | No issues | No issues |

Stable SDK checks also include clean formatting, the platform test policy and two
real Chrome HTTP checks covering Arabic/cookies and cancellation before headers.
The runnable modern example was checked without an endpoint, so it prints usage
without making a request. CI repeats minimum/stable VM, analyzer fixtures, full
Chrome and real browser HTTP checks on Linux.

### Upstream comparison

The pinned baseline contains 1,011 Vitest registrations, including 45
TypeScript type-assertion cases, plus separate `.test-d.ts` assertions. All are
mapped. The audit links 966 to actual passing Dart tests, with zero missing,
failed, skipped, title-only or orphan runtime mappings.

The other 45 registrations have explicit static/language adaptations. Two were
runtime-invalid JavaScript connection configurations: required named Dart
constructors now reject them during analysis. Actual negative fixtures verify
both partial and mixed modes; metadata/test names alone are not evidence.
Mapping categories overlap and are not additional test counts.
See [parity-summary.json](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/seifalmotaz/tanstack-ai-dart/main/validation/parity-summary.json).

The existing upstream scenarios retain their assertions through explicit legacy
entry points where the JavaScript signature itself is under test. New Dart API
tests exercise the same engine through typed construction, state streams, typed
message input, immutable state and configuration setters. Generation tests cover
value/stream/HTTP variants, persistence metadata, bad HTTP status and cancellation
of a quiet stream. Part-view tests cover exhaustive switching, unknown wire fields
and nested read-only data.

[API_COMPATIBILITY.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/seifalmotaz/tanstack-ai-dart/main/API_COMPATIBILITY.md) records all 247 upstream exports;
all 67 runtime exports remain reachable through public package barrels. This is
behavior/protocol compatibility, not identical JavaScript call signatures or
TypeScript conditional/literal/tuple inference.

Host interfaces are tested with controlled implementations. Real microphone,
WebAuthn, device storage and MCP host integration were not exercised. WebSocket
connections require an injected platform factory. No pub.dev publication was
performed. [MIGRATION.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/seifalmotaz/tanstack-ai-dart/main/MIGRATION.md) lists the pre-publication breaking changes.


## Contribution rules

Source: [CONTRIBUTING.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/seifalmotaz/tanstack-ai-dart/main/CONTRIBUTING.md)

## Contributing

Contributions to the Dart client are welcome. Start with a small reproduction or
a focused proposal in [GitHub issues](https://github.com/seifalmotaz/tanstack-ai-dart/issues).
Search existing issues and pull requests before starting overlapping work.
Use [Discussions](https://github.com/seifalmotaz/tanstack-ai-dart/discussions)
for usage questions. Follow the [community guidelines](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/seifalmotaz/tanstack-ai-dart/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md), and
use [private reporting](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/seifalmotaz/tanstack-ai-dart/main/SECURITY.md) for vulnerabilities.

### Keep the API idiomatic Dart

Preserve the official client's behavior and wire protocol while using Dart
constructors, named parameters, enums, sealed types, and streams. Avoid untyped
unions or inference wrappers added only to reproduce JavaScript syntax.
Keep unknown JSON fields intact and update public imports when adding an API.

The supported upstream revision comes from
[upstream_api.json](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/seifalmotaz/tanstack-ai-dart/main/tool/upstream_api.json),
[upstream_tests.json](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/seifalmotaz/tanstack-ai-dart/main/tool/upstream_tests.json), and
[compatibility records](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/seifalmotaz/tanstack-ai-dart/main/tool/upstream_api_compatibility.json). The Dart release
version is independent of the npm versions. Read
[the upstream update procedure](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/seifalmotaz/tanstack-ai-dart/main/doc/maintainers/upstream-updates.md) before
changing a baseline.

### Set up

You need Git, Dart at the minimum version in [pubspec.yaml](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/seifalmotaz/tanstack-ai-dart/main/pubspec.yaml), and
Chrome for browser tests. Ordinary SDK work does not require Node, pnpm, or model
provider credentials. Node and pnpm are needed only when running the official
TypeScript project for an upstream comparison.

```sh
git clone https://github.com/seifalmotaz/tanstack-ai-dart.git
cd tanstack-ai-dart
dart pub get
```

### Verify a change

Run focused tests while developing. Before requesting review, run the relevant
checks below and state which commands you actually executed:

```sh
dart format --output=none --set-exit-if-changed lib test tool example
dart analyze
dart run tool/verify_platform_test_policy.dart
dart test --platform vm --reporter json > .dart_tool/tests.jsonl
dart run tool/verify_types.dart
dart run tool/parity_audit.dart .dart_tool/tests.jsonl .dart_tool/parity.json
dart test --platform chrome
dart run tool/verify_browser.dart
dart run tool/docs.dart check
```

CI tests the minimum and stable Dart SDKs on the VM. Browser checks run on
stable. `verify_browser.dart` uses a local HTTP server, not production.
Tests that import `dart:io` must declare `@TestOn('vm')`.

Positive and negative analyzer fixtures live under `test/types`. Negative files
are intentionally invalid, excluded from normal analysis, and verified by
`tool/verify_types.dart`. Add one when an API promises a new static guarantee.

### Preserve behavioral evidence

For a bug, add a deterministic regression test that fails before the fix.
For an upstream case, keep its identity in the appropriate mapping JSON and
review its assertions against the pinned source.

A runtime mapping must name a Dart test that ran and passed. Test counts and
matching titles are not proof. Record language adaptations separately, with real
analyzer fixtures where Dart enforces a contract statically. Keep unimplemented
behavior visible instead of changing its status to make an audit green.

Use local fixtures and controlled hosts. Sanitize bug reports and avoid live
provider calls, customer data, or credentials in tests and logs.

### Update documentation and examples

Start at [doc/README.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/seifalmotaz/tanstack-ai-dart/main/doc/README.md). Edit Dart examples under `example/`,
then refresh the generated documentation:

```sh
dart run tool/docs.dart generate
dart run tool/docs.dart check
```

Only marked snippet/compatibility blocks and `llms.txt`/`llms-full.txt` are
generated. Edit the surrounding Markdown normally. Register a new guide in
`tool/docs.dart` and link it from `doc/README.md`. The check command validates
inline local link targets and generated content; it does not test remote websites.

For API changes, update examples, public compatibility records, type fixtures,
`CHANGELOG.md`, and affected guides. Add migration instructions when callers must
change usage. Change upstream inventories only when reviewing a new upstream
baseline, not to describe a Dart-only API refactor.

### Submit a pull request

Keep one change or closely related set of changes per PR. Explain the resulting
behavior, include the reproduction or motivation, and report executed checks and
remaining limits. Use the [PR template](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/seifalmotaz/tanstack-ai-dart/main/.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md).

AI assistance is welcome. Contributors remain responsible for understanding,
reviewing, and verifying submitted work. Describe material AI assistance in the
PR, and do not submit unreviewed bulk changes.

The project uses the [MIT license](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/seifalmotaz/tanstack-ai-dart/main/LICENSE). Preserve upstream attribution in
[THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/seifalmotaz/tanstack-ai-dart/main/THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES) when adapting code or tests.
Maintainers review releases using the [release guide](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/seifalmotaz/tanstack-ai-dart/main/doc/maintainers/releasing.md).


## Update the TypeScript port

Source: [doc/maintainers/upstream-updates.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/seifalmotaz/tanstack-ai-dart/main/doc/maintainers/upstream-updates.md)

## Update the port from TypeScript

Use this procedure when the official [TanStack AI repository](https://github.com/TanStack/ai)
changes. An npm release or new commit is a review candidate, not an automatic
compatibility upgrade. The Dart package version and upstream npm versions are
separate.

The checked-in [test inventory](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/seifalmotaz/tanstack-ai-dart/main/tool/upstream_tests.json),
[export inventory](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/seifalmotaz/tanstack-ai-dart/main/tool/upstream_api.json), and
[compatibility records](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/seifalmotaz/tanstack-ai-dart/main/tool/upstream_api_compatibility.json) identify the
current baseline. The README's generated table displays that pin.

### 1. Capture an immutable candidate

Use an isolated checkout. On the first review:

```sh
mkdir -p .dart_tool
git clone https://github.com/TanStack/ai.git .dart_tool/upstream-ai
```

On subsequent reviews, inspect the checkout and stop if it contains work you
need to preserve. From the Dart package root:

```sh
test -z "$(git -C .dart_tool/upstream-ai status --porcelain)" || exit 1
git -C .dart_tool/upstream-ai fetch origin
upstream_candidate=$(git -C .dart_tool/upstream-ai rev-parse origin/main)
printf '%s\n' "$upstream_candidate"
git -C .dart_tool/upstream-ai checkout --detach "$upstream_candidate"
```

To target a release instead, fetch its tag and resolve that tag to a full commit
SHA before checkout. Record both the tag and SHA. Do not assume the current npm
dist-tag and the current `main` branch point to the same source.

Read `.nvmrc`, `package.json`'s `packageManager`, and `CONTRIBUTING.md` at the
candidate. Install the Node/pnpm versions that candidate specifies. Do not reuse
an old guide's toolchain versions without checking them.

### 2. Review the changed surface

With Node available, obtain the current pin from the Dart repository's manifest:

```sh
upstream_baseline=$(node -p "require('./tool/upstream_api.json').commit")
git -C .dart_tool/upstream-ai diff --stat "$upstream_baseline" "$upstream_candidate"
git -C .dart_tool/upstream-ai diff "$upstream_baseline" "$upstream_candidate" -- packages/ai-client/src packages/ai-client/tests packages/ai/src packages/ai-event-client packages/ai-utils
```

Read relevant changes rather than limiting the review to version numbers.
Include dependency/protocol changes outside `ai-client` when they alter client
behavior. Server provider implementations remain outside this Dart client's
scope, but their wire/protocol changes may affect it.

Record added, removed, and renamed exports and test cases. Review source files
and declarations behind re-exports, including `src/index.ts`, `src/byok.ts`, and
`src/ui.ts`. Explain whether removed upstream functionality should remain as a
Dart compatibility path or requires a breaking migration.

### 3. Run the official checks

From the isolated upstream checkout, follow that candidate's contributing guide.
For the currently pinned repository, the relevant commands are:

```sh
cd .dart_tool/upstream-ai
pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
pnpm run build:all
mkdir -p .dart_tool
pnpm --filter @tanstack/ai-client test:lib --run --reporter=json --outputFile=../../.dart_tool/ai-client-vitest.json
pnpm --filter @tanstack/ai-client test:types
cd ../..
```

The report path is relative to `packages/ai-client`, so the JSON report lands in
`.dart_tool/upstream-ai/.dart_tool/ai-client-vitest.json`. Confirm the file exists
and the commands passed. If candidate scripts or configuration changed, adjust
the commands using that source and record the commands actually executed.

Run relevant protocol/dependency tests too when the reviewed change reaches
those packages. Keep Vitest runtime registrations, Vitest type assertions, and
separate `.test-d.ts` declarations distinct. Record failures and skips rather
than treating a partial upstream run as a new passing baseline.

### 4. Port behavior and update evidence

1. Add or adapt a Dart regression for each changed client behavior.
2. Implement the change using the Dart API's existing types and conventions.
3. Preserve unknown wire fields, cancellation, replay, persistence, and
   approval/interrupt ordering where the upstream contract requires them.
4. Update each affected case mapping with reviewed assertions and the real Dart
   test name. Add analyzer fixtures for representable static guarantees.
5. Describe adaptations and unsupported language/host behavior honestly.

There is no checked-in upstream inventory collector today. Review exports and
executed test results to update `tool/upstream_api.json` and
`tool/upstream_tests.json`. Do not invent a collector command or use
`parity_audit.dart` as one; the audit consumes those inventories and mappings.
A future collector must preserve test identity and prove its output against
actual source/results before replacing this manual step.

Do not silently discard renamed or deleted cases. Record the change in the PR
and changelog. Keep gaps explicit. If the port is incomplete, retain the old
supported baseline and open a draft/partial update rather than publish a claim
for the candidate.

### 5. Advance the pin in one reviewed change

Once relevant behavior is implemented and tested, update together:

- The commit and package versions in both upstream inventories and compatibility
  records. Read npm versions from the candidate's package files.
- The relevant mapping JSON, declared fixture/source hashes, and type fixtures.
- `API_COMPATIBILITY.md`, the aggregate `validation/parity-summary.json`, and
  `VALIDATION.md` with actual evidence. Copy aggregate values from the new audit
  report; do not label historical results as a fresh run.
- `PARITY.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`, and `MIGRATION.md` where behavior or public usage changed.
- `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES` when adapted source attribution changes.

Run the [contribution checks](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/seifalmotaz/tanstack-ai-dart/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#verify-a-change), including
minimum/stable SDK CI, Chrome, static fixtures, and the mapping audit. Then run:

```sh
dart run tool/docs.dart generate
dart run tool/docs.dart check
```

The docs check rejects mismatched manifest pins and stale generated compatibility
or LLM content. It does not prove behavioral parity on its own.

### 6. Request review and release separately

Include old/candidate SHAs, npm versions, changed exports/cases, assertion
reviews, actual test commands/results, and any remaining adaptations in the PR.
Changes to the pin require the same review as runtime changes. Test totals or
matching names cannot replace evidence.

Merge the reviewed port before preparing a release using the
[release guide](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/seifalmotaz/tanstack-ai-dart/main/doc/maintainers/releasing.md). This procedure changes no upstream repository,
creates no scheduled update bot, and does not publish to pub.dev.


## Release the Dart package

Source: [doc/maintainers/releasing.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/seifalmotaz/tanstack-ai-dart/main/doc/maintainers/releasing.md)

## Release the Dart package

This guide is for maintainers publishing a reviewed Dart release. It does not
publish anything automatically. GitHub source releases and pub.dev publication
are separate steps.

### Prepare the release commit

1. Finish the intended changes and review CI on the exact commit to release.
2. Set the Dart version in `pubspec.yaml` and document changes in `CHANGELOG.md`.
   Do not copy an npm version number into the Dart package version.
3. Review examples and migration instructions for public API changes.
4. Check the upstream pin against the inventories and compatibility records.
   Use the [upstream procedure](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/seifalmotaz/tanstack-ai-dart/main/doc/maintainers/upstream-updates.md) if the supported source changed.
5. Preserve [LICENSE](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/seifalmotaz/tanstack-ai-dart/main/LICENSE) and
   [THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/seifalmotaz/tanstack-ai-dart/main/THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES).

Run the applicable checks in [CONTRIBUTING.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/seifalmotaz/tanstack-ai-dart/main/CONTRIBUTING.md), then:

```sh
dart run tool/docs.dart generate
dart run tool/docs.dart check
dart doc
dart pub publish --dry-run
```

Keep installation instructions specific to the target release and regenerate
LLM references when they change. Avoid time-sensitive publication claims in an
archive that cannot be edited later. Announce hosted availability only after
publication has been confirmed.

Review the archive listing and warnings. Generated documentation, examples,
license/notice files, and public guides should be included as intended. Local
caches, fixtures with private data, and SDK downloads must stay out of the
archive. Confirm a clean working tree before the final dry run.

`VALIDATION.md` records executed evidence and untested host boundaries. A build,
HTTP status, or successful dry run does not prove real hardware integration or
that publication has occurred.

### Choose a Dart version

Use patch releases for compatible fixes and documentation corrections. Use minor
releases for compatible additions. Before 1.0, put breaking API or backend
protocol requirements in the next minor release and provide migration notes.
After 1.0, use a major release for breaking changes. An upstream pin advance is
not automatically a breaking Dart change; review both the API and wire contract.

### Publish manually

For the first release, confirm package-name availability and the intended
pub.dev publisher/ownership. A maintainer with the appropriate publishing access
must approve and perform the release. CI does not publish packages.

From the reviewed clean release commit:

```sh
dart pub publish
```

Confirm the version, archive, license, and repository link on pub.dev. Only after
that confirmation should release announcements claim hosted availability.

### Create a GitHub source release

A GitHub source release can precede publication to pub.dev. Keep those statuses
separate in the README and release notes. Verify all CI checks on the immutable
source commit before creating its tag. Write reviewed release notes to
`.dart_tool/release-notes.md`, and set `release_commit` to that verified SHA.
For the first source release:

```sh
release_tag=v0.3.0
test -n "$release_commit" || exit 1
git tag -a "$release_tag" "$release_commit" -m "tanstack_ai_dart $release_tag"
git push origin "refs/tags/$release_tag"
gh release create "$release_tag" llms.txt llms-full.txt --verify-tag --title "$release_tag" --notes-file .dart_tool/release-notes.md --latest
```

If a tag already exists, verify its target instead of overwriting it. Derive attached files from that exact source revision.
For versioned LLM copies, rebase only this repository's GitHub/raw URL references
from `main` to the release tag; preserve examples and compatibility data. Include
checksums for attached files. A release's LLM text provides a versioned
reference alongside GitHub's automatic source archives.

### Record the release

When publishing to pub.dev, use the same reviewed source commit as its GitHub
release, or create a new release/version if the source changed.
Include the Dart version, supported upstream versions/SHA, migration notes, and
validation scope. Do not reuse an upstream npm tag as the Dart release tag.

The [application integration checklist](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/seifalmotaz/tanstack-ai-dart/main/NEXT_STEPS.md) covers host-specific
work that consuming applications still own. No mobile store upload or production
application deployment is part of this library release.


## Community guidelines

Source: [CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/seifalmotaz/tanstack-ai-dart/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md)

## Code of Conduct

This is a small community project around an unofficial Dart SDK. Participation
is open to anyone who treats others with basic respect.

### Expected behavior

- Disagree about technical decisions directly and respectfully. Critique code,
  evidence, and tradeoffs, not people.
- Assume good faith and keep discussion focused on the project.
- Welcome contributors with different experience levels and time zones.

### Unacceptable behavior

- Harassment, threats, discrimination, or personal targeting.
- Spam, promotional noise, or repeated off-topic posting.
- Publishing someone's private information without consent.
- Sustained disruption of issues, pull requests, or discussions.

This applies to issues, pull requests, discussions, and other project spaces.

### Moderation

Maintainers may moderate, close, or lock abusive or off-topic content, and may
limit participation when needed. Moderation is proportionate and does not
require a formal escalation process.

### Reporting

Use GitHub's "Report content" or "Report abuse" tools on the specific content
or profile, documented at
https://docs.github.com/en/communities/maintaining-your-safety-on-github/reporting-abuse-or-spam
For contribution expectations, including AI-assisted work, see
[CONTRIBUTING](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/seifalmotaz/tanstack-ai-dart/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).


## Security reporting

Source: [SECURITY.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/seifalmotaz/tanstack-ai-dart/main/SECURITY.md)

## Security

This is an unofficial community Dart SDK for TanStack AI, not affiliated with TanStack.

### Reporting a vulnerability

Use GitHub's private vulnerability reporting and open a draft advisory at:

https://github.com/seifalmotaz/tanstack-ai-dart/security/advisories/new

Use this private channel for sensitive reports. Do not include credentials, API
keys, customer prompts, or other private data. Provide a minimal reproduction.

Report ordinary bugs in [GitHub issues](https://github.com/seifalmotaz/tanstack-ai-dart/issues).
Ask usage questions in [Discussions](https://github.com/seifalmotaz/tanstack-ai-dart/discussions).

### What to include

- A minimal, sanitized reproduction.
- The affected Dart SDK version and package version.
- Platform and runtime details (Dart, OS, browser or VM).
- The observed impact and any conditions required to trigger it.

### Supported versions

Fixes are reviewed against the latest GitHub release only. Older versions do not
carry a separate maintenance promise. The initial release is v0.3.0; the Dart
version is independent of any npm package pin.

See [LICENSE](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/seifalmotaz/tanstack-ai-dart/main/LICENSE) for warranty terms and
[CONTRIBUTING](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/seifalmotaz/tanstack-ai-dart/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for how changes are proposed and verified.
